chapter.heading: An Appeal for Israel’s RepentanceTo the Chief Musician. On an instrument of Gath. A Psalm of Asaph.
chapter.v:
Sing aloud
to God our strength;Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob. [Is. 21:2; Hab. 2:8 (Gen. 37:34). (11:2; 42:1; 61:1; Ezek. 36:26, 27; Joel 2:28, 29) who originates] [Rev. 13:10 c Is.]

Raise a
song and strike the timbrel,The pleasant harp with the lute. [Is. 25:9; 26:8]

Blow the
trumpet at the time of the New Moon,At the full moon, on our solemn feast day. [Is. 17:13]

For this
is a statute for Israel,A law of the God of Jacob.

This He
established in Joseph as a testimony,When He went throughout the land of Egypt,Where I heard a language I did not understand. [Ps. 97:9]

“I removed
his shoulder from the burden;His hands were freed from the baskets.

You called
in trouble, and I delivered you;I answered you in the secret place of thunder;I tested you at the waters of Meribah.Selah [2 Kin. 18:18,]

“Hear,O My
people, and I will admonish you!O Israel, if you will listen to Me! [Judg. 5:6 i 2 Kin. 18:13-17]

There shall
be no foreign god among you;Nor shall you worship any foreign god. [Is. 24:4]

I am
the Lord your God,Who brought you out of the land of Egypt;Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it. [Ps. 12:5; Is.]

“But My
people would not heed My voice,And Israel would have none of Me. [[Ps. 7:14; Is. 26:18; 59:4; James]

So I
gave them over to their own stubborn heart,To walk in their own counsels. [Is. 9:18]

“Oh,that My
people would listen to Me,That Israel would walk in My ways! [Ps. 48:10; Is. 49:1]

I would
soon subdue their enemies,And turn My hand against their adversaries. [Is. 30:27, 30; Heb. 12:29]

The haters
of the Lord would pretend submission to Him,But their fate would endure forever.

He would
have fed them also with the finest of wheat;And with honey from the rock I would have satisfied you.”
